name: Cloud
description: The minimal-agent cloud connector. Owns the network transport to the cloud backend and registers it into the host transport registry, so Intercom's peers and teams transparently span machines without Intercom importing this plugin. Skeleton: the remote transport is a stub (no live connection) until the backend auth contract lands. Tool: CloudStatus.

tool.name: CloudStatus
tool.description: Report the minimal-agent cloud connector status: whether cloud features are enabled, the current feature flags, and whether the remote transport is registered into the host transport registry. Calling it also ensures the (stub) remote transport is registered (idempotent). Read-mostly. Example: CloudStatus({}).

tool.name: CloudLogin
tool.description: Log this CLI into the minimal-agent cloud backend using the device-authorization grant (RFC 8628). Prints a short user code + a verification URL to approve in your browser, then completes the login and saves the access token locally so cloud features (teleport, remote peers, teams) turn on. Configure the backend with MINIMAL_AGENT_CLOUD_URL (default http://localhost:4000/api/auth). Example: CloudLogin({}).

tool.name: CloudPush
tool.description: Manually upload this session's new records to the cloud teleport store so it can be viewed live from web or mobile. Idempotent and resumable: only records the cloud hasn't seen are sent. Requires being logged in (CloudLogin) with cloud features enabled; otherwise it's a no-op. Uploads also happen automatically in the background between turns. Example: CloudPush({}).
